examples.label: Example · The quarters are the halfway light

body.t: At first and last quarter the illumination is exactly 50% in the model — half the disc lit — even though the phase is a quarter of the cycle. The names count the cycle; the percent counts the light. Confusing them is the oldest Moon mistake.

The model returns 100% for 3 March 2026 — the date of a total lunar eclipse, which can only happen at full. And about 1% for 12 August 2026, the solar-eclipse date. Extremes landing on eclipse dates is how the model earns trust.

faq: Why does a 'half moon' show 50% at the quarter?

Because the geometry agrees for once: at the quarters, exactly half the visible disc is sunlit. The quarter names the cycle position (a quarter and three-quarters around), the percent names the light — they coincide at 50% by design of the sphere.

In the mean model, at the full-moon instant. In the real sky the Moon usually passes slightly north or south of perfect alignment, so true illumination kisses 100% briefly — eclipses are the rare exact hit.
Does my hemisphere change the percent?
No — illumination is a whole-Earth property at an instant. Hemispheres change the lit side's orientation (the Moon looks mirrored from Australia), never the fraction.
Very — within a day or two of full the difference is subtle. Landscape brightness depends more on the Moon's altitude: a high 70% Moon out-lights a low 95% one dragging through murk.
Why is the crescent's dark side sometimes faintly visible?
Earthshine: sunlight reflected off Earth lights the Moon's night side softly — 'the old Moon in the new Moon's arms'. It is strongest near new, when Earth is fullest as seen from the Moon.
Can illumination be negative or over 100?
No — the fraction is bounded by the geometry. Tools that say '-3% lit' are showing a signed phase convention, not this fraction.
How does this pair with moonrise times?
Percent tells how much light; rise and set tell when it is available. A 95% Moon that sets at 21:00 leaves a dark late night — the two tools together are the full forecast.
